title: Clean stale branches and enforce branch hygiene
purpose: Remove branches that are proven safe to delete and automatically delete future same-repository pull-request head branches after closure, while preserving main, open pull-request branches, and unproven orphan branches.
invariants: The default branch is never deleted.
A branch backing an open pull request is never deleted.
An unmerged branch with no closed pull-request evidence is retained as an orphan for explicit review.
The cleanup code executed with write permission is always checked out from the default branch, never from a pull-request head.
The workflow has no merge authority and changes no repository content.
Every deletion and retention decision is recorded in a machine-readable workflow artifact.
requiredEvidence: branch hygiene workflow executes from main after merge
machine-readable inventory of deleted, retained-open, retained-orphan, and failed branches
no open pull-request branch is deleted
adversarialTests: prove open pull-request branches are retained
prove an unproven orphan branch is retained
prove a closed pull-request head branch is eligible for deletion
treat already deleted refs as idempotent success
reject execution outside the declared repository context
nonGoals: delete unproven orphan branches without an explicit closure record
independentReview: explicit closure review of the two retained smoke branches

automaticEvents: main push changing the workflow or cleanup engine

acceptance.finalExpectedBranchState: main-only when no pull request is open
acceptance.residualCondition: GitHub administrative ruleset configuration remains tracked separately by issue 27.

rollback: Revert the workflow, script, documentation, and work package. Deleted branch names are not recreated automatically, but their commits remain recoverable through merged or closed pull-request history where applicable.
